Yes — almost certainly.

At your stated time and location, the Moon is:

- **About 15° above the eastern horizon** (azimuth ~87°, nearly due east)
- **~98% illuminated**, so essentially a full Moon
- In a **clear night sky**
- With the Sun **more than 30° below the horizon**, so twilight is not a problem

A nearly full Moon at that altitude is extremely conspicuous to normal unaided vision. Look low in the **east**, roughly a fist-and-a-half held at arm’s length above a level horizon (one fist is about 10°). It may be somewhat affected by haze, trees, buildings, or local light pollution because it is still low, but if you have a reasonably open eastern view, you should be able to spot it easily.
